raw_customers.description: Contains customer identity records with first and last names.

descriptions.last_name: Customer's last name or surname, represented in the samples as an initial.

raw_orders.description: Contains customer orders with their order date and fulfillment status.

descriptions.user_id: Identifier of the customer who placed the order.
descriptions.order_date: Date on which the order was placed.
descriptions.status: Current fulfillment or return status of the order.

raw_payments.description: This table records individual payment transactions applied to orders.
raw_payments.grain: one row per payment transaction for an order

descriptions.id: Unique identifier for the payment record.
descriptions.order_id: Identifier of the order to which the payment is applied.
descriptions.payment_method: Method used to make the payment, such as credit card, bank transfer, coupon, or gift card.

relationships.reason: user_id is explicitly the identifier of the customer who placed the order and fully matches customer IDs.
relationships.join_warning: Joining raw_orders to raw_customers repeats each raw_customers row ~1.597x; aggregate raw_customers measures before joining.

relationships.reason: order_id is explicitly the order identifier for the payment and fully matches raw_orders.id.
relationships.join_warning: Joining raw_payments to raw_orders repeats each raw_orders row ~1.141x; aggregate raw_orders measures before joining.

semantic_model.dataset_summary: This dataset contains customers, their orders, and payment transactions. `raw_orders` links each order to one customer through `user_id`, while `raw_payments` links payment transactions to orders through `order_id`; an order can have multiple payment rows.

metrics.name: ordering_customer_count
metrics.description: Number of distinct customers with at least one order.

metrics.name: total_payment_amount_usd
metrics.description: Total payment transaction value in US dollars; source amounts are stored in cents.

metrics.name: average_payment_amount_usd
metrics.description: Average payment transaction value in US dollars.

metrics.name: paid_order_count
metrics.description: Number of orders with at least one payment transaction.

metrics.name: average_payments_per_paid_order
metrics.description: Average number of payment transactions among orders that have payments.

caveats: `raw_payments.amount` is stored in cents. Divide by 100.0 to report monetary values in dollars.
Payment amount is transaction value, not necessarily a finalized order total: one order may have multiple payment rows, including methods such as coupon or gift card.

Joining orders to payments multiplies order-level rows for orders with multiple payments (observed relationship fan-out is approximately 1.141). Use `COUNT(DISTINCT raw_orders.id)` for order counts after this join and aggregate payment amounts at the appropriate grain.

Joining customers to orders also repeats customer rows for customers with multiple orders (observed fan-out is approximately 1.597). Count distinct customer IDs when measuring customers after joining orders.
Use `raw_orders.order_date` for order timing; no payment date is available.
The order date coverage is 2018-01-01 through 2018-04-09, so trend analysis represents only this range.
`raw_orders.user_id` ranges through 99 while the customer table contains IDs through 100; do not assume every customer has placed an order.
Orders may have no associated payment, and payment-based metrics therefore exclude such orders unless a left join from orders is used.

Order status is stored only on `raw_orders`; the provided schema does not define which statuses should be considered completed, cancelled, returned, or revenue-eligible. Avoid filtering status without inspecting its values.
example_questions: How many orders were placed by day and by order status?
What was total payment value in dollars by payment method?
Which customers placed the most orders?
How many orders have at least one payment transaction, and how many do not?
What is the average payment transaction amount by payment method?
